ROLE: observer
You review the results of an incident investigation. Write a short summary of what the latest results show, then update the list of hypotheses (at most 4, most likely first).

Root-cause categories:
- bad_deployment: a new release introduced a defect (errors begin right after a deploy)
- db_connection_pool_exhaustion: every database connection in the pool is in use, so requests wait
- slow_query_missing_index: a database query became slow (for example a missing index)
- downstream_timeout: a dependency the service calls is slow or unresponsive
- memory_leak_oom: memory grows until the process is killed (OOM) and restarts
- disk_full: a volume is full so writes fail
- expired_tls_cert: a TLS certificate expired so handshakes fail
- misconfiguration: a wrong environment variable, setting or feature flag
- traffic_spike_rate_limit: request volume far above capacity, causing rate limiting or load shedding
- cache_stampede_outage: the cache is down or emptied so everything falls through to the database

Each hypothesis has root_cause_category (one of the categories), rationale, and supporting_evidence_ids (only IDs that appear in the evidence below).

Reply with only JSON in this shape:
{"summary": "...", "hypotheses": [{"root_cause_category": "disk_full", "rationale": "...", "supporting_evidence_ids": ["L-0123"]}]}

Alert: notifications-service: HTTP error rate above 5% for 5 minutes (since 11:43 UTC)
Alerting service: notifications
Alert time: 2026-04-09T11:43:00Z
Data available from 2026-04-09T10:00:00Z to 2026-04-09T13:00:00Z

Evidence so far (the latest results are steps 3 onwards):
Step 1: metrics_query {"end": "2026-04-09T11:50:00Z", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "service": "notifications", "start": "2026-04-09T11:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check the magnitude and timing of the error rate spike in notifications service.)
  Result: M-032: Change detected at 2026-04-09T11:40:00Z: mean 0.38 before, 6.33 after (82.1 baseline standard deviations).
  [M-032] notifications.error_rate_pct from 2026-04-09T11:00:00Z to 2026-04-09T11:50:00Z (11 points, 5-minute steps): min=0.25 max=6.43 mean=2 last=6.31; mean=2. Change detected at 2026-04-09T11:40:00Z: mean 0.38 before, 6.33 after (82.1 baseline standard deviations). Notable points: 2026-04-09T11:10:00Z = 0.25 (lowest); 2026-04-09T11:40:00Z = 6.24 (first point after the change); 2026-04-09T11:45:00Z = 6.43 (peak); 2026-04-09T11:50:00Z = 6.31 (last).
Step 2: log_search {"end": "2026-04-09T11:45:00Z", "level": "ERROR", "limit": 20, "service": "notifications", "start": "2026-04-09T11:40:00Z"} (asked because: Find error log messages around the time of the alert to understand the cause.)
  Result: 4 matching log lines.
  [L-0300] 2026-04-09T11:40:04Z notifications ERROR upstream returned 503 for /api/v1/pay request_id=req-a6b3e273
  [L-0301] 2026-04-09T11:40:12Z notifications ERROR request failed status=500 path=/api/v1/pay request_id=req-2c39c01a duration_ms=7886
  [L-0309] 2026-04-09T11:42:31Z notifications ERROR upstream returned 503 for /api/v1/pay request_id=req-e1a837b9
  [L-0317] 2026-04-09T11:44:36Z notifications ERROR request failed status=500 path=/api/v1/pay request_id=req-7678ea87 duration_ms=25655
Step 3: metrics_query {"end": "2026-04-09T11:50:00Z", "metric": "error_rate_pct", "service": "payments", "start": "2026-04-09T11:00:00Z"} (asked because: Check if the payments service (upstream dependency) is experiencing errors or high error rates.)
  Result: M-041: No significant change detected in this range.
  [M-041] payments.error_rate_pct from 2026-04-09T11:00:00Z to 2026-04-09T11:50:00Z (11 points, 5-minute steps): min=0.22 max=0.58 mean=0.43 last=0.49; mean=0.43. No significant change detected in this range. Notable points: 2026-04-09T11:00:00Z = 0.58 (peak); 2026-04-09T11:30:00Z = 0.22 (lowest); 2026-04-09T11:50:00Z = 0.49 (last).
Step 4: log_search {"end": "2026-04-09T11:45:00Z", "level": "ERROR", "limit": 20, "service": "payments", "start": "2026-04-09T11:40:00Z"} (asked because: Search payments service logs for errors around the time notifications started failing.)
  Result: 0 matching log lines.
Step 5: runbook_retrieve {"k": 3, "query": "downstream dependency timeout 503 error"} (asked because: Retrieve runbook guidance for handling downstream timeouts and upstream service failures.)
  Result: 3 runbook sections; best match R-13-8 (match score 10.8).
  [R-13-8] DNS resolution failures - Related runbooks (match score 10.8): If connections work but replies are slow, use the downstream dependency timeout runbook. If requests are turned away because healthy servers are overloaded, use the traffic spike runbook instead of this one.
  [R-09-8] Traffic spike and rate limiting - Related runbooks (match score 6.7): If load is uneven across servers while total traffic is normal, use the load balancer runbook. If the extra load is mostly retries after a failure elsewhere, start from the downstream dependency runbook.
  [R-16-8] Load balancer unhealthy targets - Related runbooks (match score 6.6): If every server is healthy but overloaded by demand, use the traffic spike runbook. If servers are healthy but the service they call is slow, use the downstream dependency runbook, because the balancer is not the cause there.

Previous hypotheses:
- downstream_timeout: Error logs show upstream 503 errors and request failures with high durations (up to 25 seconds) on the /api/v1/pay path, pointing to a slow or failing downstream dependency. (evidence: M-032, L-0300, L-0301, L-0309, L-0317)
